name: repair-hub
description: Self-hosted repair-reference and shop-management app. Vehicle records with VIN decode, live NHTSA recalls/complaints and EPA fuel-economy specs, a DTC (diagnostic trouble code) lookup preloaded with the ~140 generic SAE-standard OBD-II codes, and free-text search against iFixit's guide library and Wikimedia Commons for reference photos -- all backed by content you add yourself (repair guides, wiring diagrams, photos). Full shop management on top: customers, work orders, estimates with no-login customer approval (signature capture included), appointment scheduling with an .ics calendar feed, parts inventory, digital vehicle inspections, sales tax, payment tracking, warranty tracking, a technician time clock, email notifications, PDF invoices, and reports (revenue by month, average repair time, top parts, outstanding balances). Three account tiers share one login page -- staff (full access, with optional 2FA), technicians (repair reference plus only their assigned jobs), and customers (their own vehicles and service history, via a login staff can create for them). Does not scrape, mirror, or resell ALLDATA or any other paid data provider -- if you already pay for ALLDATA, a vehicle's page lets you save a quick link to the matching page in your own account, or attach a file you personally exported. All other external lookups (NHTSA, EPA, iFixit, Wikimedia Commons) are free, public APIs and degrade gracefully with no internet access. SET DJANGO_SECRET_KEY before starting -- pick any long random string. Set the superuser username and password too, or you'll have no way to log in (create one later via `docker exec -it repair-hub python manage.py createsuperuser` if you skip it here). Everything lives under the single /config mount: the SQLite database and all uploaded media (guide photos, wiring diagrams, ALLDATA attachments, inspection photos). Back that one directory up and you've backed up the whole app -- see the README for a scripted hot-backup that's safer than a raw file copy while the container is running.

paths.name: Appdata
paths.description: SQLite database and all uploaded media (guide photos, wiring diagrams, attachments) -- the only folder you need to back up

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: Unraid's nobody user -- keeps appdata editable from the host

variables.name: TZ
variables.description: Timezone for dates shown in the app

variables.name: Django Secret Key
variables.description: Required. Any long random string -- used to sign sessions/cookies. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32

variables.name: Superuser Username
variables.description: Your first login. Created automatically on first boot if this and the password below are both set.

variables.name: Superuser Password
variables.description: Required for the first login to be created. Change it in Admin after logging in.

variables.name: Superuser Email
variables.description: Optional, only used to pre-fill this account's email

variables.name: Allowed Hosts
variables.description: Comma-separated hostnames/IPs the app will answer to, or * for any (default -- fine for a LAN-only appliance). Only lock this down to specific hosts if you're exposing this through a reverse proxy on the open internet.

variables.name: Debug Mode
variables.description: Leave false unless troubleshooting -- true shows full Python tracebacks on error pages, which can leak internal details

variables.name: SMTP Host
variables.description: Optional. Set to enable real email for appointment/estimate/invoice notifications; leave blank to just log them to the container console.

variables.name: SMTP Port
variables.description: Only used if SMTP Host is set.

variables.name: SMTP Username
variables.description: Only used if SMTP Host is set.

variables.name: SMTP Password
variables.description: Only used if SMTP Host is set. Use an app password for Gmail/Outlook, not your account password.

variables.name: From Email
variables.description: Sender address on outgoing notification emails.

variables.name: Backup Interval (hours)
variables.description: How often to write an automatic JSON snapshot to /config/backups. Set to 0 to disable.

variables.name: Backup Retention Count
variables.description: How many automatic snapshots to keep before deleting the oldest.
